business: Nota (@NotaGetBot): a Telegram bot that collects receipts, invoices and handwritten delivery notes from work chats into the owner's Google Sheet and flags duplicates and arithmetic errors
by_segment: Remote investor in villas or a build, living abroad
Villa management company or villa rental operator
why_not: I would let my admin try the free 30, it costs nothing, but in a café that is gone in a week and I already pay someone to do the spreadsheet. My staff send photos to the group when they remember, and I don't believe they will change how they work just because there is a bot now.

My bookkeeper already runs everything through our expense app and it works well enough. I might forward a few receipts from the Telegram groups to see what it does, but I'm not moving my books to a bot I found this week.

I'd throw the free 30 receipts at it, sure, it costs me nothing. But I'm not paying until it catches something my own checking misses, and a new Telegram bot from nobody I know could be gone by next year.

I might throw the free 30 receipts at it to see what it does, but I'm not moving my staff and my work groups onto a little Telegram bot I've never heard of and paying monthly for it. The mess annoys me, but I only dig into it when something smells wrong, so it's not burning enough to make me pay now.

I would forward a few receipts to the free version, since that costs nothing, but I would not pay yet. Half of what my staff send are faded warung notes and handwritten nota in Indonesian, and if I end up correcting rows at midnight I might as well scroll the Telegram group like I do now.

I'd send it a few nota for free, sure, but I'm not paying until I see it read my guys' scrawled handwritten nota from the supply shop correctly. And 'forward it and forget about it' is the opposite of how I run things since I caught someone padding receipts. Excel and my own checking cost me nothing.

I make every transfer myself, so my bank statement already is the record, and I can paste the screenshots into a sheet in five minutes a week. I'd maybe use the 30 free ones out of curiosity, but I won't pay $19 a month for that.

My admin already collects the transfer screenshots and receipts from the group and types them into our sheet. $19 a month adds a bot on top of a job someone is already paid to do, so I don't see what I'd save.
why_yes: I'm abroad and the admin's sheet is always a week behind, so at midnight I'm scrolling the group chat guessing what got spent on the build. The first 30 are free with no card, a build burns through 30 notas fast, and if it reads them decently, $35 a month is nothing next to finally seeing duplicates and wrong totals the same day.
flip: Seeing it read my worst real receipts during the free 30, the handwritten and faded ones from the group, with the right totals and catching a duplicate I had missed.
If after the free documents my staff are still sending receipts to the bot on their own and my admin tells me the sheet matches what she would have typed, then I pay for the 200 plan.

If during the free 30 it reads a pile of my own messy Indonesian nota without mistakes and flags a real double-claim or a padded total I would have missed, then I'd pay the $35 without thinking twice.
If it showed me on the first free batch that my site manager's receipts don't add up to what I wired, and it cost under $10 a month or a one-off fee per build.

If my staff's actual handwritten nota from the free 30 come back with the right totals and item names nearly every time, with only a few rows to fix, I'd pay rather than build and maintain my own bot.

If it could push straight into the app my bookkeeper already uses, so the Telegram receipts stop getting lost without changing how we keep the books, and I could see a real company behind it with other Bali contractors using it for a year.
Seeing it run in our actual work group through one full month-end, so my accountant gets a complete set without me chasing anybody.
If during the free 30 it flags a real duplicate or a bad total from my scooter repairs that I missed myself, I'd pay the $19.

Another villa operator in Bali telling me they've used it for six months with their staff in the group and it hasn't missed receipts or broken. That, plus seeing it catch a real duplicate or wrong total in my own groups during the free trial.
A way to get the sheet without connecting Google at all, like a file it sends me every week, plus a clear name and company behind it that I can look up.
If my admin tried the free 30 on a week of scooter parts and fuel and told me it cut her Excel day down to almost nothing, I'd pay without thinking about it.
If the free 30 documents read my mechanics' handwritten notes and fuel slips correctly and my admin could stop the weekly typing, I'd pay the $35 tier.
Another Bali business owner I know using it in their own work group, plus a real company name and a plain answer on whether the bot can read normal chat messages or only the receipts.
My bookkeeper trying it on one site for a month and telling me it actually cut the missing documents, and that everything stays in my own Google sheet if the bot disappears.
A free full month, not 30 documents, so I see whether my staff keep using it and whether the Monday report actually catches a duplicate or a wrong total that saves me real money.
If my admin quit or kept making mistakes, and I could use it without adding it to the group chat or connecting Google, just forwarding receipts myself and exporting the sheet.
Watching it get a batch of my real handwritten supply-shop nota right and catch an actual double-claimed or wrongly added receipt that I would have missed.

Proof it will last, like a year of public track record or a clear promise that if it shuts down I keep the sheet and get the setup to run myself, plus a cheaper plan around $9 for a small shop like mine that sends maybe 60 receipts a month.
